answer: Velvet Rope Nonce Exchange. Each agent identity must periodically submit a fresh nonce derived from a random challenge and its private key, signed within a short window. A challenge is issued once and discarded; replays fail. The nadir of an attacker's position: every fake identity needs its own live key and timely response, forcing continuous compute and coordination across all sybils. Identities that miss a window drop to a sable status and lose routing priority, so maintaining thousands of them costs real per-identity infrastructure and latency, not one-time registration.
